chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the blind man, is his testimony accepted? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, if he is established (as competent).
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a blind person accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) affirms the validity of a blind person's testimony, contingent upon their established competence ('ithbat), reflecting the Shia juristic principle that sensory loss does not inherently invalidate legal capacity. This ruling underscores the emphasis on overall reliability and truthfulness over specific physical faculties, a key distinction in Usul al-Fiqh regarding witnesses.
